plan_summary: Ring Homomorphisms, Subrings, and Homomorphism Kernels
expected_source:
[\ring.homomorphism:from{R ::= (R_set, +_R, *_R, 0_R, 1_R)}:to{S ::= (S_set, +_S, *_S, 0_S, 1_S)}]
Declares: phi(x__) is \function:on{R_set}:to{S_set}
when: R, S is \ring
satisfies:
. forAll: a, b "in" R_set
  then: phi(a +_R b) = phi(a) +_S phi(b)
. forAll: a, b "in" R_set
  then: phi(a *_R b) = phi(a) *_S phi(b)
. phi(1_R) = 1_S
Documented:
. called: "ring homomorphism from $R?$ to $S?$"
. description: "A ring homomorphism $\phi : R \to S$ is a structure-preserving
                mapping between rings that respects the additive group structure,
                the multiplicative monoid structure, and identity elements:
                $\phi(a +_R b) = \phi(a) +_S \phi(b)$, $\phi(a *_R b) = \phi(a) *_S \phi(b)$,
                and $\phi(1_R) = 1_S$.
                Citations: David S. Dummit and Richard M. Foote, Abstract Algebra
                (3rd ed., John Wiley & Sons, 2004, Chapter 7, Section 7.3, p. 239);
                Serge Lang, Algebra (3rd ed., Springer, 2002, Chapter II, Section 1, p. 83);
                Nicolas Bourbaki, Elements of Mathematics: Algebra I, Chapters 1-3
                (Springer-Verlag, 1989, Chapter 1, Section 8, p. 96)."



[\subring:of{R ::= (R_set, +_R, *_R, 0_R, 1_R)}]
Declares: S ::= (S_set, +_S, *_S, 0_S, 1_S)
when: R is \ring
specifies:
. S_set \:subset:/ R_set
. +_S is \binary.operation:on{S_set}
. *_S is \binary.operation:on{S_set}
. 0_S "in" S_set
. 1_S "in" S_set
satisfies:
. 0_R "in" S_set
. 1_R "in" S_set
. 0_S = 0_R
. 1_S = 1_R
. forAll: x, y "in" S_set
  then:
  . x +_S y = x +_R y
  . x *_S y = x *_R y
. have:
  . forAll: x, y "in" S_set
    then:
    . x +_R y "in" S_set
    . x *_R y "in" S_set
  . forAll: x "in" S_set
    then:
    . exists: y "in" S_set
      suchThat: x +_R y = 0_R
  asserting: S is \ring
Enables:
. view:
  as: S' := S is \ring
Documented:
. called: "subring of $R?$"
. written: "S? \leq R?"
. description: "A subring $S \subseteq R$ is a subset of a ring $R$ containing
                the ambient multiplicative identity $1_R$ that forms a ring in
                its own right under the restricted operations of $R$.
                Equivalently, $S$ contains $0_R$ and $1_R$ and is closed under
                addition, additive inverses (subtraction), and multiplication,
                with $0_S = 0_R$ and $1_S = 1_R$.
                Citations: David S. Dummit and Richard M. Foote, Abstract
                Algebra (3rd ed., John Wiley & Sons, 2004, Chapter 7, Section
                7.1, p. 228, ISBN: 978-0471433347); Serge Lang, Algebra (3rd
                ed., Graduate Texts in Mathematics 211, Springer, 2002,
                Chapter II, Section 1, p. 84, ISBN: 978-0387953854); Nicolas
                Bourbaki, Elements of Mathematics: Algebra I, Chapters 1-3
                (Springer-Verlag, 1989, Chapter 1, Section 8, Definition 3,
                p. 97, ISBN: 978-3540642435)."



[\ring.kernel:of{phi(x__)}:from{R ::= (R_set, +_R, *_R, 0_R, 1_R)}:to{S ::= (S_set, +_S, *_S, 0_S, 1_S)}]
Defines: K := \set@{x_ : x_ "in" R_set | phi(x_) = 0_S}
when:
. R, S is \ring
. phi is \ring.homomorphism:from{R}:to{S}
Documented:
. called: "kernel of $phi?$"
. written: "\ker(phi?)"
. description: "The kernel of a ring homomorphism $\phi : R \to S$ is the preimage
                of the additive zero of the codomain, $\ker(\phi) = \{x \in R \mid \phi(x) = 0_S\}$.
                Citations: David S. Dummit and Richard M. Foote, Abstract
                Algebra (3rd ed., John Wiley & Sons, 2004, Chapter 7, Section
                7.3, Definition p. 240, ISBN: 978-0471433347); Serge Lang,
                Algebra (3rd ed., Graduate Texts in Mathematics 211, Springer,

                1-3 (Springer-Verlag, 1989, Chapter 1, Section 8, Section 8.1,
                p. 99, ISBN: 978-3540642435)."



Theorem:
given:
. R ::= (R_set, +_R, *_R, 0_R, 1_R) is \ring
. S ::= (S_set, +_S, *_S, 0_S, 1_S) is \ring
. phi is \ring.homomorphism:from{R}:to{S}
where:
. K := \ring.kernel:of{phi}:from{R}:to{S}
then:
. K is? \ideal:of{R}
Documented:
. called: "Kernel of a Ring Homomorphism is an Ideal"
. description: "The kernel of any ring homomorphism $\phi : R \to S$ forms a
                two-sided ideal of the domain ring $R$.
                Citations: David S. Dummit and Richard M. Foote, Abstract
                Algebra (3rd ed., John Wiley & Sons, 2004, Chapter 7, Section
                7.3, Proposition 6, p. 240, ISBN: 978-0471433347); Serge
                Lang, Algebra (3rd ed., Graduate Texts in Mathematics 211,
                Springer, 2002, Chapter II, Section 1, Theorem 1.1, p. 85, ISBN:
                978-0387953854); Nicolas Bourbaki, Elements of Mathematics:
                Algebra I, Chapters 1-3 (Springer-Verlag, 1989, Chapter 1,
                Section 8, Proposition 1, p. 99, ISBN: 978-3540642435)."
Proof: """
Let $R = (R_{\text{set}}, +_R, *_R, 0_R, 1_R)$ and $S = (S_{\text{set}}, +_S, *_S, 0_S, 1_S)$ be rings,
and let $\phi : R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism.
By definition, the kernel is
$$ K = \ker(\phi) = \{x \in R_{\text{set}} \mid \phi(x) = 0_S\}. $$
To establish that $K$ is an ideal of $R$ ($K \text{ is } \operatorname{ideal}(R)$),
we verify the defining conditions:

1. **Non-emptiness and Zero Element**:
   Since $\phi$ is a ring homomorphism, it preserves the additive group structure:
   $$ \phi(0_R) = \phi(0_R +_R 0_R) = \phi(0_R) +_S \phi(0_R). $$
   Subtracting $\phi(0_R)$ from both sides in the abelian additive group of $S$ gives:
   $$ \phi(0_R) = 0_S. $$
   Therefore, $0_R \in K$, so $K$ is non-empty.

2. **Additive Subgroup**:
   Let $x, y \in K$, which implies $\phi(x) = 0_S$ and $\phi(y) = 0_S$.
   Because $\phi$ is a homomorphism between the underlying additive abelian groups of $R$ and $S$,
   it respects additive inverses: $\phi(-_R y) = -_S \phi(y) = -_S 0_S = 0_S$.
   Thus:
   $$ \phi(x -_R y) = \phi(x +_R (-_R y)) = \phi(x) +_S \phi(-_R y) = \phi(x) -_S \phi(y) = 0_S -_S 0_S = 0_S. $$
   Consequently, $x -_R y \in K$.
   By the one-step subgroup test, $K$ is an additive subgroup of $(R_{\text{set}}, +_R, 0_R)$.
   In particular, $K$ is closed under addition ($x +_R y \in K$ for all $x, y \in K$)
   and additive inverses (for each $x \in K$, there exists $y \in K$ such that $x +_R y = 0_R$).

3. **Absorption / Two-Sided Ideal Property**:
   Let $r \in R_{\text{set}}$ and $x \in K$. Since $x \in K$, $\phi(x) = 0_S$.
   Using the multiplicativity of the ring homomorphism $\phi$:
   - For left multiplication:
     $$ \phi(r *_R x) = \phi(r) *_S \phi(x) = \phi(r) *_S 0_S = 0_S, $$
     which proves that $r *_R x \in K$.
   - For right multiplication:
     $$ \phi(x *_R r) = \phi(x) *_S \phi(r) = 0_S *_S \phi(r) = 0_S, $$
     which proves that $x *_R r \in K$.

Since $K$ contains $0_R$, is closed under subtraction, and absorbs multiplication by all elements of $R$ from both the left and right, $K$ forms a two-sided ideal of $R$.
"""
